subject: Clarify decision roles & next steps — LumenAI evaluation
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@lumenai.com>, Rajesh Rao <rajesh@lumenai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + who signs / budget owner?

Hi Olivia (and team),

Great to meet you on the call earlier — thanks for walking through the LumenAI evaluation priorities. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we keep momentum: 

Key points I captured from the discussion:
- Primary decision criteria: latency < 80ms p95, per-token cost target, and SSO + audit log requirements for regulated data.
- Evaluation window: pilot for 6–8 weeks to validate latency and cost under peak traffic.
- Security gates: SOC 2 evidence + data retention policy requested by legal.

Asks / next steps:
1) Can you confirm the economic buyer and the person who owns the budget for this initiative? (We heard Rajesh might be involved but wanted to confirm.)
2) Introduce procurement/legal contact so we can route the security questionnaire and share a short evidence packet.
3) Proposed 15–30 minute intro with the econ buyer to align success criteria and purchasing cadence — please share availability.

I attached a short cost estimate and a privacy summary to help frame procurement questions. I also included a one-page technical checklist we use for pilots.

Attachments: redwood-brief-cost-estimate.pdf, redwood-privacy-summary.pdf

If helpful, I can draft a 2-line intro you can forward to Rajesh and procurement.

Thanks,
Hannah

A few clarifications from our side:
- Confirmed: Rajesh Rao (CFO) is the economic buyer for platform spend related to AI infra. I'll copy him for visibility.
- Procurement contact is procurement@lumenai.com (shared inbox).

I've attached our vendor evaluation criteria spreadsheet to give you a sense of how procurement scores proposals.
